title: Granularity determined by spectral sparsity
statement: Let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional cube over $ bf_2$ to signs, and suppose the spectral sparsity $s$ of the real-valued function $x\mapsto f(x)$ is greater than $1$. Then this function is vector Fourier granular with granularity $2^{1-\lfloor\log_2 s\rfloor}$; each Fourier coefficient on the sign cube is an integer multiple of this number.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional $ bf_2$ cube to signs
The spectral sparsity of $x\mapsto \operatorname{signValue}(f(x))$ is greater than $1$
